# audit-branch

Deeply evaluate one change-set — a branch, a revision range, or the staged / working-tree diff — and hand the human a shareable HTML decision page: an independent summary of what the changes actually do beside the branch's own claims, plus numbered findings from six angles — **trap**, **integration**, **usage**, **intent**, **coverage**, **craft**, defined under "What the clean-room evaluation does" — each with an apply-ready patch. The evaluation runs in a **clean room** (`claude -p` from a `/tmp` room) so project memory and the branch's own persuasive prose cannot bias it; the code lenses read **comment-stripped** copies, and every lens holds whole files, base originals, traced callers, and tests — never just the diff hunks. You (the in-session orchestrator) do only mechanical work, the human gates, and the human-watched apply.

**Device-library scope — the embedded lens leads.** When the changed files live under `libraries/`, `/audit-embedded` is the **primary** lens and this audit's standards findings defer to it: size and allocation cost — flash bytes, import-time RAM, hot-path allocations, class / def / exception count, string-constant weight — outrank docstring completeness, defensive guards, rich error prose, and well-formedness. A finding that *adds* code to a device library to satisfy a standard (a guard, a docstring section, an error taxonomy, a speculative API) must justify its bytes; if it can't, downgrade it to advisory and rank it below every size finding. The inversion applies only under `libraries/` — standards stay primary for `scripts/`, `workbench/`, `.claude/surfaces/`, and the skills themselves. Measured 2026-07-05 baseline and the cut campaign: [`plans/workstreams/library-size-cut.md`](../../../plans/workstreams/library-size-cut.md).

## Inputs and modes

- **change-set**: a branch name (diffed from its `origin/main` merge base), an explicit `<base>..<head>` range, `--staged` (the index vs HEAD), or `--worktree` (uncommitted edits vs HEAD). The orchestrator resolves what the user said and confirms scale before running.
- **`--repo <root>`** (optional): audit a different git repo. Append it to every `branch_phase0.py` / `branch_phase1.py` call and run every `git` command as `git -C <root>`. `apply_fix.py runtests` derives the repo root from the patched file's path; no flag needed. Every workspace-flavored rule (the VERSION-bump check, the preflight-awareness gate names, the cross-runtime apply gate) carries a `REPO-SPECIFIC (ChuMicro)` marker at its site — one grep finds everything to delete or convert when these skills are ported.
- **`--voice <key>`** (optional): the register the findings are written in, from the shared registry (`../_shared/voices/voices.json`). Default **`plain`**. A voiced run grounds the writer with the voice's real-prose excerpt (persona-only when none exists). If omitted, print the in-session voice menu and let the user pick.
- **`--intent <text-or-path>`** (optional): supplements the intent record when the commit messages undersell the purpose — a workstream file, a ticket's text, or one typed sentence. Commit messages of the range are always included; staged/worktree changes have none, so `--intent` matters most there.
- **Model:** every clean-room layer runs on **opus** (the lenses do cross-file reasoning and the validator gates each finding).

## Invariants (do not violate)

**MUST READ:** [`../_shared/clean-room-pipeline.md`](../_shared/clean-room-pipeline.md) — the nine invariants every clean-room audit run obeys (clean room + deny rules, lens blindness by named inputs, single interactive layer, eval-first gated apply, user-global memory out, no auto-commit, push-back forks, background + Monitor, reader findings outrank the orchestrator). Numbered references like "invariant 8" in this file point there. This skill's deltas:

- **Lens → file map (invariant 2):** trap, integration, usage, and coverage read comment-stripped copies; the intent and craft lenses read the commented `head/` tree on purpose (the intent record and prose drift are their material) — keep the lens prompts in `branch_wf.js` exact when editing them.
- **The summarizer never sees the intent record.** Its read of the diff is the independent description the human compares the branch's claims against; feeding it the commit messages would collapse that check. It also reads only stripped copies — new docstrings are the branch's claims in prose form.
- **Read-only against git.** Base and head content come from `git show` blobs — the skill never checks out, rebases, or mutates refs, and the working tree changes only in the apply loop, only in files the human picked.
- **Extra push-back fork (invariant 7):** a **very large range** — state the file count and that lens attention dilutes past ~20 files (*Audit the full range · Narrow to one package · Split into per-package runs*).
- **Usage-path lens (invariant 1's sanctioned exception):** step 4b is this skill's in-session judging layer.
- **Backgrounded commands (invariant 8):** `branch_phase0.py`, `branch_phase1.py`, and `usage_trace.py validate`; the watch is `python3 $PIPE/progress_watch.py <room…>`.

## Procedure

### Runbook (the orchestrator follows these literally; the notes below explain the clean room)

Let `SKILL` = the **absolute** path of this skill's directory, `PIPE=$SKILL/../audit-code` — the clean-room pipeline home this skill shares (rooms, preflight, stripper, progress watcher, voices, apply helper) — and `CONT=$SKILL/../_shared/audit_continuity.py`, the continuity keystone (persistence, baseline carryover, the waiver ledger, incremental carry). Absolute, because in `--repo` mode the audited repo, not this workspace, is the natural cwd. `<slug>` = a filesystem-safe name for the change-set: the branch name, or `staged` / `worktree`. Allocate every room with `rooms.py new <slug>` — never hand-build a `/tmp` path; two runs guess the same name and collide.

0. **Preflight (in-session):** `python3 $PIPE/preflight.py --expect-email <the account THIS session runs as>`. **STOP on a failure or an ACCOUNT MISMATCH:** show the preflight output, name expected vs actual account, state the consequence (every clean-room layer runs and bills under the CLI account, not this session's), then gate with `AskUserQuestion` (*Proceed as the CLI account · I'll re-login first · Cancel*).
   - *Success:* `claude` is present, logged in, and the CLI account matches the session (or the user explicitly picked Proceed).
1. **Resolve the change-set (in-session):** map the user's words to a mode + refs — a branch name → `BASE=$(git merge-base origin/main <branch>)`, `HEAD=<branch>`; "since `<ref>`" or an explicit range → that range; "staged" / "uncommitted" → `--staged` / `--worktree`. Nothing concrete → `AskUserQuestion` (*Staged changes · Working tree vs HEAD · I'll name a range*). Then show `git --no-pager diff --stat` for the resolved set, state the file count, and confirm; past ~20 files push back on cost and dilution (invariant 7). When `--intent` was not given, try to discover the intent record (REPO-SPECIFIC (ChuMicro)): grep the range's commit subjects for `plans/workstreams/` paths or `Phase N` sentence topics and offer the matched workstream file as `--intent`; in `--staged` / `--worktree` mode offer the `plans/next-up.md` bullets touching the changed packages. A discovered record rides only with the user's nod. When nothing is discovered and the mode is `--staged` / `--worktree`, ask in chat (free-form, not an `AskUserQuestion`): "What is this change supposed to do? One sentence, a ticket, or a workstream path — or say skip." Pass the answer to step 4 as `--intent`; on skip, tell the user the intent lens and the claims column will run empty.
   - **Prior-run detection (agent-driven — the user never forms the baseline):** glob the persistence tree for an earlier audit of this same change-set — `python3 $CONT find-prior --root <repo>/.scratch/audits --slug <slug>`. A `PRIOR …` hit (vs `NO-PRIOR`) is carried **two** ways, both without a user action, the user only ever seeing stamped cards: **(a) baseline** — announce it plainly ("found a prior audit of this branch from `<date>`, carrying it as baseline") and pass `--baseline <prior>/eval.json` to `render_branch.py` at step 5, so every card is stamped new / persisting / resolved and any prior skip-with-note is preloaded; **(b) incremental** — resolve the change-set to the **delta range** `<prior head_sha>..<head>` (the `head_sha` is in the prior run's `persisted.json`) so the lenses pay only for the files changed since the last audit, and pass `--carry-from <prior_dir>` to `branch_phase1.py` at step 4, which carries the prior findings on the *unchanged* files forward via a cheap re-check instead of a fresh lens pass and tracks what resolved. Baseline carryover is agent-driven, never user-formed. (REPO-SPECIFIC (ChuMicro): `.scratch/audits/` is the persistence tree; in `--repo` mode use the destination the user gave at persist time.)
   - *Success:* mode + refs stated with the diff stat shown, the user confirmed the scope, and any prior run was detected and announced (or `NO-PRIOR` — a first audit, run full).
2. **Feature context (clean room, background — launch it now; it needs no voice):** default ON when the change-set spans more than one package or more than 5 changed `.py` files, OFF otherwise — state which way the heuristic fell and why, and take the user's override in either direction. When ON: `ROOM0=$(python3 $PIPE/rooms.py new <slug>-facts)`, then launch `python3 $SKILL/branch_phase0.py <base> <head> $ROOM0` (or `--staged` / `--worktree`) with `Bash(run_in_background: true)` and arm a non-persistent `Monitor` on `python3 $PIPE/progress_watch.py $ROOM0 --until FEATURE_FACTS.md` — never a foreground watch or a poll loop → a ledger of the pre-change world (feature, contracts, glossary). It runs while step 3 talks to the user. Announce the heuristic and launch immediately when ON — don't block on a reply. An override arriving after launch: OFF → stop the phase-0 task with `TaskStop` and proceed without facts; ON → launch it late and let step 4 wait on it.
   - *Success:* `FEATURE_FACTS.md` exists with non-empty FEATURE, CONTRACTS, and GLOSSARY sections — or the step was skipped / degraded and the user was told which.
3. **Voice gate (in-session, overlaps step 2):** if `--voice` was given, use it. Otherwise print the full menu — `python3 $PIPE/voices.py menu` — then gate with `AskUserQuestion` (header "Voice"): *plain — voiceless, clearest (default) · cantrill — names what is fragile, good for traps · another voice from the menu above (name it via Other)*. The printed menu carries the full registry; the structured gate carries the default.
   - *Success:* a voice key is fixed.
4. **Evaluate (clean room, background):** wait for step 2's phase-0 task to finish if it launched — if it ended without producing `FEATURE_FACTS.md` (its output prints a WARNING), tell the user and proceed without `--facts` — then `RUN=$(python3 $PIPE/rooms.py new <slug>)` and `python3 $SKILL/branch_phase1.py <base> <head> $RUN --voice <key> [--intent <text-or-path>] [--facts $ROOM0/FEATURE_FACTS.md] [--carry-from <prior_dir>]` (or `--staged` / `--worktree` in place of the refs). On an incremental run (step 1 found a prior audit), `<base> <head>` is the delta range `<prior head_sha>..<head>` and `--carry-from <prior_dir>` folds the prior findings on unchanged files into the ledger; the phase's completion summary reports how many were carried and how many resolved since. The launcher also stages the waiver ledger's file-relevant slice into the room (`waivers.json`) so the merger's actionability gate can suppress a finding a human already skipped-with-a-note, and after collection marks any such suppression deterministically — a finding is suppressed only when a real ledger entry matches its fingerprint. **Launch with `Bash(run_in_background: true)` (invariant 8)** after telling the user what is running and the rough duration (*"summarizer + 6 lenses + merger + validator loop + patch/voice pass, clean room, several minutes"*). It stages the diff, head/base/stripped copies, traced usage files, tests, the intent record, and the facts ledger, then runs the workflow. Read the `=== BRANCH AUDIT PHASE COMPLETE ===` summary; note unconfirmed findings and any usage files `usage_map.json` dropped over the staging cap. **0 findings AND 0 file summaries means the run degraded:** read `$RUN/phase1.json`, `$RUN/claude_envelope.json` (the headless result envelope — it names a rate-limit / auth / refusal cause and the run's cost), and the background task's output to name which layer degraded, tell the user, and gate the re-run with `AskUserQuestion` (*Re-run the evaluation · Show the room artifacts · Stop*).
   - *Success:* the completion summary was read; `eval.json` carries findings (or a genuine zero with a non-empty `summary.json`), patches were generated, and convergence was noted.
4b. **Usage-path lens (in-session, deliberately no clean room):** while step 4 runs, ask where the changed code is consumed — `AskUserQuestion` (*This repo only · Also consumer repos — paths via Other · Skip the trace*) — then `python3 $PIPE/usage_trace.py trace --root <repo> [--root <consumer> …] --seeds-from $RUN/changed_symbols.json --out $RUN/usage_paths.json` (wait for the seeds file first — `python3 $PIPE/progress_watch.py $RUN --until changed_symbols.json`; staging writes it within seconds of the step-4 launch, but the consumer-repos gate can resolve faster) — callers, then callers of callers, until its caps (depth 4 · 40 files; every stop is recorded and named in the report). Callers are **jedi-resolved, not name-matched**: `--seeds-from` anchors each changed `Class.method` to its own file and def, and `goto` confirms every candidate site, so a changed generic method traces to its real call sites instead of tripping a name cap. Needs `jedi` (pinned in `requirements-dev.txt`; `python scripts/run.py setup` installs it). After step 4 completes: `Workflow(scriptPath: $PIPE/usage_path_wf.js, args: {pathsFile: $RUN/usage_paths.json, roomDir: $RUN, seeds: [<from the trace output>]})` — a feature mapper summarizes what the traced code serves, one judge per seed walks its chains on **full commented code**, and a writer composes the prose in the room's voice. `Write` the returned JSON to `$RUN/path_findings.json`, launch the blind cross-check `python3 $PIPE/usage_trace.py validate $RUN $RUN/path_findings.json` with `Bash(run_in_background: true)` (invariant 8 — it wraps one silent clean-room `claude -p`) and proceed on its completion notification. Run it by default; skipping is the user's call, never the orchestrator's — gate a skip with `AskUserQuestion` naming the stakes (*Run the blind check — N path cards get a verdict · Skip — N cards land on the page unvalidated*). Then `python3 $PIPE/usage_trace.py merge $RUN $RUN/path_findings.json`. The in-room usage lens covers direct callers blind; this lens goes past the first hop on real code — the judges skip what the ledger already carries.
   - *Success:* `usage_paths.json` holds ≥1 edge or a recorded stop, path findings (possibly zero) merged with the feature map, and the blind check ran or the user chose to skip it — or the user skipped the trace.
5. **Render + serve (in-session):** when the usage-path trace ran, start only after step 4b's merge lands — the page renders once, complete. First run the generated repros — `python3 -m pytest $RUN/repros/repro_<id>.py`, one file at a time: FAIL demonstrates its finding; PASS means the defect does not reproduce, so treat that finding as *discuss* at the gate and say so (a repro that just ran red also satisfies step 7's pre-edit red run). Then `python3 $SKILL/render_branch.py $RUN [--baseline <prior>/eval.json]` → `$RUN/picker.html`: page-top context (feature facts, the independent what-it-does read, the branch's own claims, per-file change summaries with finding back-links), then one severity-ordered list of folded finding cards narrowed by severity / angle chips and a file dropdown. When step 1 found a prior run, pass `--baseline` yourself (the user never forms it): every card gains a **status chip** — `new` leads un-greyed, `persisting` / `resolved` / `waived` render greyed so attention goes to what changed — a `status` facet joins the bar, resolved findings show as greyed ghost cards, and any prior skip-with-note is preloaded as a skip with the note shown. Serve with `python3 $SKILL/../../../.claude/surfaces/serve_picker.py $RUN` as `Bash(run_in_background: true)` — it posts the page to the repo's surface hub, which owns the one browser tab (never `open` the URL yourself and never set `PICKER_NO_OPEN`; withdraw a question the conversation has moved past via `python3 -m surfaces.hub withdraw <id>`, or re-serve with `--supersede`) — then arm a **persistent** `Monitor` (`persistent: true`; stop it with `TaskStop` once the selection lands) running `tail -f` on the serve task's **output file** (the path the backgrounding response printed) — a non-persistent Monitor's default 5-minute timeout outlives no human review, and the selection blob arrives through this watch. Surface `$RUN/eval.json` (the durable, diffable findings record) and the self-contained `$RUN/picker.html` (the shareable report itself) by stating their absolute paths in chat. **Tell the human what to look at:** the finding counts, the top one or two, the repro outcomes (demonstrated red vs did-not-reproduce), any validator-unconfirmed items (they default to *discuss*), and whether the usage trace hit its cap. Offer to persist the run — `python3 $CONT persist $RUN --into <repo>/.scratch/audits --slug <slug>` copies the whole findings substrate (eval / written / patches / summary / validation / picker.html, plus `manifest.json` for the head SHA, and — re-run after step 6 — the `selection.txt` blob) into `.scratch/audits/<slug>-<UTC>/` and stamps a `persisted.json` (head SHA + UTC). The /tmp room dies with the machine; this persisted copy is the substrate every continuity feature reads — baseline carryover, the waiver ledger's provenance, and the incremental delta all start here, so persisting is what makes the *next* audit cheaper and quieter. (REPO-SPECIFIC (ChuMicro): `.scratch/` is this workspace's gitignored scratch tree; in `--repo` mode ask the user for a destination.)
   - *Success:* `picker.html` rendered with one card per `eval.json` finding, served, the URL opened, the persistent Monitor armed, `eval.json` + `picker.html` paths surfaced, and the human pointed at the page with a plain-language summary.
6. **Selection gate (in-session, human):** the human picks per finding — *apply / discuss / skip*, plus notes — and submits (the blob arrives as a Monitor event), pastes the copied selection, or types ids in chat (`3, 7, 12` = apply these). Parse the selection with `python3 $PIPE/apply_fix.py parse-selection <blob-file>` (it normalizes `<id> = <choice>` lines, `note <id>:` riders, and bare-number lists), echo the parsed vector before acting, and talk through each *discuss* pick before any change. A submitted vector that matches the page defaults untouched gets a confirm before applying (*"You submitted the defaults unchanged — apply the N pre-picked fixes?"*) — pre-picked radios are a policy hint, not a human choice. An all-skip selection is valid — fire an `AskUserQuestion`: *Done — apply nothing · Re-read, I'll pick after · Pick fixes now*.
   - **Record a waiver for each skip-with-note (in-session):** when the human **skips** a finding *and leaves a note* — an "intentional, here's why" — write it to the central ledger: `python3 $CONT record-waiver --run $RUN --id <finding_id> --note "<the human's exact words>"`. The command pulls the finding's fingerprint (file + symbol + defect) from `$RUN/eval.json` and appends one line to `plans/audit-waivers/ledger.jsonl`. On a later audit of this code the ledger's actionability gate suppresses that finding with the quoted note, so a reasoned skip stops resurfacing as noise. Record a waiver **only** for a skip that carries a genuine reason (a bare skip is "not now", not "never"); never for an *apply* or *discuss*. A note on an *apply* is a wording adjustment, not a waiver.
   - *Success:* a per-finding choice vector (possibly all skip) + notes captured and echoed in chat; each skip-with-note recorded as a waiver.
7. **Guarded apply loop (in-session) — only if ids were selected:** `python3 $PIPE/apply_fix.py plan $RUN <ids>` prints each selected finding with its ready-made patch; the patch's `file` names the edit target (a changed file, or a caller for a usage finding — caller patches may be `manual` with guidance, because callers were staged comment-stripped). Walk the fixes **one at a time, gating each**: a finding whose patch carries a **repro** (`$RUN/repros/repro_<id>.py`) runs it BEFORE the edit expecting **FAIL** (an already-passing repro means the defect does not reproduce — surface that instead of applying); apply with `Edit` (re-read and adjust when an earlier fix shifted the `before`); re-run the repro expecting **PASS**; run `python3 $PIPE/apply_fix.py runtests <that file>` (pytest, then the repo apply gate when `../_shared/apply_gate.py` defines one for the file — in this workspace a `libraries/` or `support/` fix also gates on that package's cross-runtime suite), surface a red suite instead of continuing, show `git --no-pager diff -- <changed files>`, then move on. A red repro also upgrades a validator-unconfirmed finding to demonstrated — run it before that push-back and say so in the question. After a repro-gated fix lands green, offer to adapt that repro into the package's own test suite — a red→green repro is exactly the pinning test the coverage lens hunts for. (REPO-SPECIFIC (ChuMicro): adaptation means the cross-runtime `tests/` lane — plain asserts, no `import pytest` — so offer the translation, never a verbatim copy.) Leave everything **uncommitted**; honor invariant 7's push-backs.
   - *Success:* each applied fix was a human-watched edit gated by its repro when one exists (red before the edit, green after) and by its own pytest run (reported pass/fail) and a shown diff; nothing was committed.

### What the clean-room evaluation does (Step 4, inside `branch_phase1.py` → `branch_wf.js`)

The lens prompts in `branch_wf.js` are the source of truth for each lens's charter; this section is a summary — edit both in the same commit. The launcher stages the room mechanically — no judgment: the merge-base diff, head-side copies (commented and stripped), base-side stripped copies, every repo file referencing a changed symbol (found by `git grep` per symbol, capped and recorded in `usage_map.json`), the changed modules' located tests, the range's commit messages as `intent.txt`, and the `FEATURE_FACTS.md` ledger when step 2 produced one. One `claude -p` then runs: a **summarizer** + **six lenses** in parallel, a **merger** into a numbered fact ledger, a **validator loop**, and a **compose pass** (writer in voice + patcher). Every lens **and the summarizer** may consult the facts ledger when staged — it describes the pre-change world, never the branch's claims; the summarizer's blindness is to `intent.txt`, not to the facts.

- **Summarizer** (diff + stripped base + stripped head, intent-blind): what the change-set actually does, overall and per file — the description the human checks the branch's claims against.
- **Trap lens** (stripped head + diff): where the change makes behavior wrong — inversions, boundary errors, mis-referents traced across methods, swallowed errors, plus the hazards a change can open (peer-sized allocations, untrusted data reaching a sensitive sink, check-then-act gaps), with a run-it-in-your-head pass over edge inputs.
- **Integration lens** (stripped base vs head): the public surface's compatibility across three classes — call (a base-era call fails at head), behavior (same signature, moved semantics), contract evolution (a relied-on invariant dropped) — plus the repo's VERSION-bump rule (REPO-SPECIFIC (ChuMicro) — marked in `branch_wf.js` for porting). A break the diff itself fully migrates is not a finding. Integration judges the surface in the abstract — no callers are staged for it; concrete call sites belong to the usage lens, and the merger folds the pair into one finding when both fire on the same name.
- **Usage lens** (stripped callers + stripped head): every traced call site judged against the new behavior — broken assumptions, newly-raised exceptions unhandled, changed defaults, removed names. Judges only staged callers; the cap is surfaced, never guessed past.
- **Usage-path lens** (in-session, step 4b — the deliberate exception): traces the changed symbols' transitive callers (and any consumer repos the user names) with `usage_trace.py` — jedi-resolved call sites anchored to each changed symbol's real def, so even a changed generic method traces precisely — maps the **features** the traced code serves, and judges the full commented chains for behavior the change ripples into hops away. The judges **risk-sample the contract edges** (error paths, boundary/sentinel values, cross-library seams) rather than enumerating every call site; findings land in feature terms, file under their own `path` angle chip carrying the in-session marker, and pass a blind clean-room cross-check before merging into the ledger. The in-room usage lens owns the first hop; this lens owns everything past it.
- **Intent lens** (diff + intent record + commented head): the two-gate drift policy — flag only divergence the intent record does not acknowledge; stated narrowing / expansion / re-approach is accepted scope. Past the gates: root-cause-vs-symptom on claimed bugfixes (a guard above an unfixed corruption is a finding), unrelated riders, and commit messages that misdescribe their own diff. Also mines the claims worth showing the human as context.
- **Coverage lens** (stripped head + diff + tests): new or altered behavior only — what no test exercises, what no test pins (the change could silently regress), tests updated to bless the new output without re-derivation, hollow new tests.
- **Craft lens** (commented head + diff): changed regions only — prose the change broke (docstrings now wrong, stale comments, contradicted docs), new code that reads wrong, inconsistency with the surrounding file's idiom.
- **Merger:** consolidates into the fact ledger (telegraphic `defect` / `bite` / `fix` fragments, stable integer ids) behind an actionability gate — a finding must name something to change and carry a file + symbol + quoted site; praise, "please verify", and unanchored guesses are dropped. The same gate consults the staged `waivers.json`: a finding matching a human waiver (same file + symbol + the waived defect) is **kept but marked `suppressed`** with the waiver's quoted note — a suppression that always traces to a recorded human decision, never the orchestrator's authority (this is how invariant 9 stays intact under re-audit: the ledger, not the reviewer-in-the-loop, silences a finding). `branch_phase1.py` re-applies the same fingerprint match deterministically after collection, so a waived finding never slips through when the merger misses it.
- **Validator (fixture-agnostic):** re-checks every finding against the diff, code, callers, and tests — is the defect real at head, is the bite honest, would the fix work — and re-runs the merger until clean or 4 attempts. What stays flagged is marked **unconfirmed**.
- **Writer + patcher:** the writer composes title / consequence / problem / fix fresh from the fragments in the chosen voice, grounded by the voice's real-prose excerpt in `voice_sample.txt` when one exists; the patcher emits an apply-ready `replace` / `add` / `manual` patch per finding, each naming its file — plus, for trap/usage/integration findings a test can demonstrate, a **repro**: a self-contained pytest that fails at head and passes once the fix lands, written to `$RUN/repros/` for the apply loop's red→green gate (the clean room has no Bash, so in-session is where they execute).

All lenses carry the **preflight-awareness rule**: never flag what this repo's deterministic gates already catch (ruff lint, failing tests, coverage percentages) — the lenses hunt what automated checks cannot detect. (The gate names are REPO-SPECIFIC (ChuMicro), marked in `branch_wf.js`; the concept ports as-is.)

## Done when

- `picker.html` was rendered with one card per `eval.json` finding, served, and opened; the `eval.json` and `picker.html` paths were surfaced to the user.
- The page carries the independent summary of what the changes do, the branch's own claims beside it, and numbered findings across the six clean-room angles — plus the in-session path angle when the usage-path trace ran — each leading with a plain consequence, carrying a mechanism, a suggested fix, a patch naming its file, and a confidence, validator-converged or marked unconfirmed, in the chosen voice.
- The human was pointed at the page with the counts and the top items, and told whether the usage trace hit its staging cap.
- Any selected fixes were applied as human-watched `Edit`s, each gated by the affected file's tests and a shown `git diff`, and left uncommitted.
- Nothing was committed automatically; no ref was checked out or mutated.
- No clean-room layer ran with `--add-dir` into the project, the isolation flags (`--setting-sources project,local --strict-mcp-config --disable-slash-commands`) kept user-global memory out, no code lens saw a comment, and the summarizer never saw the intent record.

## Reference files

- `branch_phase0.py` — optional feature-context pass: stages the affected packages' base-side stripped sources and runs one clean-room `claude -p` → `FEATURE_FACTS.md` (feature / contracts / glossary of the pre-change world).
- `branch_phase1.py` — the evaluation phase: resolves the change-set (`<base> <head>`, `--staged`, `--worktree`), stages diff + head/base/stripped copies + traced usages + tests + the intent record, runs `branch_wf.js` as one clean-room `claude -p`, and collects `eval.json` / `written.json` / `summary.json` / `validation.json` / `patches.json` / `phase1.json`. `--stage-only` stops after staging, for debugging and the TESTPLAN rows.
- `branch_wf.js` — the evaluation workflow (summarizer + 6 lenses → merger with the actionability gate → fixture-agnostic validator loop → writer + patcher). Findings and patches carry a `file`; every agent dispatch inside passes `model: 'opus'` explicitly (the launcher's `--model` flag binds only the top-level loop); the orchestrator substitutes `__RUNDIR__` (done by the launcher).
- `render_branch.py` — builds `spec.json` from the run room and renders `picker.html` via the shared picker: context sections up top, folded severity-ordered cards behind severity / angle chips and a file dropdown. `--baseline <prior eval.json>` stamps every card new / persisting / resolved against a prior run (greying carried cards, adding a `status` facet, showing resolved ghost cards, preloading a prior skip-with-note) — the orchestrator passes it; the user never forms it.
- `../_shared/audit_continuity.py` — the continuity keystone shared with audit-code: one **fingerprint** (file + symbol + normalized defect token-set, drift/rename tolerant, never line numbers) used four ways — baseline stamping, prior skip-with-note preloading, waiver-ledger matching, and incremental carry. CLI: `persist` (copy a run's substrate into `.scratch/audits/<slug>-<UTC>/`), `find-prior` (newest persisted run for a slug + its head SHA), `record-waiver` (append a skip-with-note to the ledger). `plans/audit-waivers/ledger.jsonl` is the central committed waiver registry (one JSON line per waiver: quoted note + fingerprint + date); its `README.md` documents the format. (REPO-SPECIFIC (ChuMicro): the ledger home and the `.scratch/audits/` persistence tree are workspace conventions.)
- Shared pipeline (`$PIPE` = `../audit-code/`): `rooms.py` (fresh-room allocation), `preflight.py` (CLI + account guard), `strip.py` (comment stripper), `progress_watch.py` (Monitor-friendly artifact watcher), `voices.py` (voice registry access), `usage_trace.py` + `usage_path_wf.js` (the step-4b usage-path lens: trace via jedi reference resolution / blind validate / merge, and the in-session judge workflow — its mapper/judge/writer dispatches pin `model: 'opus'`; `trace` needs `jedi`, pinned in `requirements-dev.txt`), `apply_fix.py` (`plan` + `parse-selection` + `runtests` — pytest, then the repo apply gate when `../_shared/apply_gate.py` defines one; that gate file is the single repo-specific seam, replaced or deleted wholesale when these skills are ported to another repo). Serving + submit loop-back: `.claude/surfaces/serve_picker.py`.
- `TESTPLAN.md` — the empirical validation rows for the bundled scripts (mechanical staging, end-to-end, human gates, trigger probes).

## Patterns to avoid

- Judging from the diff hunks alone — the lenses hold whole files, base originals, callers, and tests because a one-line change breaks invariants far from the hunk; a hunk-only read is the failure mode this skill exists to beat.
- Treating commit messages as ground truth — they are claims; only the intent lens reads them, as claims, and the summarizer is kept blind to them.
- Re-flagging what preflight already catches (lint, style, failing tests, coverage numbers) — noise that buries the findings only this skill can produce.
- Locating a finding by raw line number — stripped copies shift them; locate by the finding's `file` + `symbol` + quoted code.
